newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit remains soft on offshore dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit remains soft on offshore dollar demand.

text.p: The ringgit remained soft in Asian trading on Wednesday on dollar buying by offshore players, dealers said.
The ringgit was also pressured by rumours of a large Malaysia's trade deficit for April, they said.
"Rumours were circulating that April deficit could be as large as two billion ringgit. But the market is slowly discounting it," said a dealer at a large Malaysian bank.
Economists were expecting an April deficit of less than 500 million ringgit. Malaysia posted a trade surplus of 1.75 billion ringgit in March.
Dealers said the market was cautious at 2.5190/5200, the level Bank Negara was said to have checked rates last Wednesday.
"Except for a firmer dollar, there has been no basic fundamental change to suggest that the ringgit should weaken to above 2.5200," said research house MMS International.
Dealers said they expected heavy offers of dollar/ringgit from local players at 2.5200.
Apart from trade figures, the market was also awaiting April monetary supply figures, which could provide some clues to the country's interest rate direction, dealers said.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5175/85 a dollar against 2.5160/70 at the close of Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.
